purpose: Version-pinned verification of every third-party thing Maestro depends on: the agent CLIs it drives (B06) and the Python distributions it declares (B17). A row records what was checked, against which exact version, on what date, and where the raw observation is retained. maestro/thirdparty.py compares each row against what is installed; maestro doctor --thirdparty is the gate. See docs/DESIGN.md section 15.

records.subject: agy
records.verified_by: P07B headless probe at 1.2.2 (agy models, --effort vocabulary, json/stream-json output, --conversation resume; ~20K input tokens of the gemini pool per real turn) plus a zero-quota re-check at 1.2.3: `agy --version`, `agy models`, and an --effort probe that fails client-side before any turn

effort_control.observed: --effort accepts low|medium|high only on a base id (gemini-3.8-flash); a suffixed id already fixes the effort and any other --effort conflicts with it, and claude-* rejects --effort outright. The vocabulary is per model, which a per-backend EffortControls cannot express, so no native_values are recorded and maestro selects effort through the model id.

findings.resume: verified at 1.2.2: --conversation <id> continued the same conversation (num_turns 2, step_index continued). The id cannot be set at launch; the driver recovers it from the stream-json init event in impl.log.
findings.compaction: no compact command or hook exercised; auto-checkpoint thresholds come from ~/.gemini/model_context_limits.md (140K Flash family, 128K 3.1 Pro ceiling, 80K GPT-OSS), not re-measured
findings.usage_surface: headless json/stream-json carries per-turn tokens (input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens) but no quota and no CLI version. Quota is only in ~/.gemini/statusline_dump.json, a four-pool `quota` object (gemini-5h, gemini-weekly, 3p-5h, 3p-weekly) written by the operator's interactive status line.
findings.quota_measurement: push-only: no headless pull path. The driver reads statusline_dump.json and reports both quotas on Usage.pools -- gemini-5h/gemini-weekly under usage_pool_id `antigravity-gemini`, 3p-5h/3p-weekly under `antigravity-3p` (P12A S2). Usage.windows stays the Gemini pools alone, the driver's one headline account reading, so a 3p exhaustion never reads as Gemini pressure. The catalog gives claude-* / gpt-oss-* profiles the 3p pool and BackendCapabilityEntry.pool_for routes admission on it.
findings.sandbox_mode: observed 2026-09-16 at 1.2.3 (P12A S2, two bounded headless probes in a scratch git repo, rc 0 both): maestro's own completion_argv shape (`--output-format json --model <id> -p <prompt>`) edited a workspace file with NO permission prompt and NO permission flag, and the same run under `--sandbox` still wrote to the workspace. `--sandbox` therefore runs non-interactively but restricts the *terminal*, not the filesystem -- matching `--help` -- so the driver keeps declaring sandbox=false, which means 'can constrain filesystem/network access'. Re-observed 2026-09-17 at 1.2.4 (bounded edit+shell probes, gemini-3.8-flash-low): `--mode accept-edits` changed nothing observable -- under this host's ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json `toolPermission: always-proceed`, file edits and shell commands ran in both modes with no denied_actions. The real hazard was the workspace: without `--add-dir <cwd>` the system prompt says "The user does not have any active workspace", run_command takes a model-chosen Cwd, and 2 of 6 probes (one per mode) wrote their file and ran their command in $HOME. The driver now passes `--add-dir <cwd>` on launch, resume and completion; 3 of 3 probes then stayed in the cwd. It also passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` on every run (Dan, 2026-09-17: agy runs unattended like the other agents), so the host toolPermission setting no longer matters; verified headless, edit and command ran, no denied_actions.

open_questions: A quota-exhaustion error string was never observed; parse_exit matches maestro's generic limit regex against non-agent output only.
Effort values are per model, not per backend; an effort label must never be mapped across vendors without a measured mapping (B06).
records.notes: Driven by maestro/backends/antigravity.py (registry name `antigravity`, catalog backend_id `antigravity_cli`) and kept out of the implicit fallback chain (DriverRef.in_default_chain=False). Routing judgement lives in maestro/backends/catalog.py ANTIGRAVITY_CATALOG_DEFAULTS: only gemini-3.8-flash-high is balanced; every other id is light.

records.subject: claude
records.verified_by: local blind-spot audit (scripts/graph_blind_spot_audit.py) re-run against the installed CLI on 2026-09-13 (help_controls, maestro_capabilities and usage shape unchanged from 2.1.269) — --help inspection and two repeated Maestro telemetry reads, no agent turn

quota_surface.five_hour_resets_at: present — a real epoch in every sampled reading, where 2.1.263 returned null
quota_surface.seven_day: present — used_pct and a real resets_at, where 2.1.263 returned null
quota_surface.context_reading: context_used_pct and context_total_input_tokens are both populated; 2.1.263 reported 0 tokens and a null pct
quota_surface.attribution: account-level; the sample now names a model ("Opus 5") but that is the reading session's model, not an attribution of the measured delta to one invocation

effort_control.observed: claude --help at 2.1.272 (2026-09-15): `--effort <level>  Effort level for the current session (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)`. The canonical low/medium/high are native words, so no mapping is declared.

open_questions: Maestro declares sandbox=false while the installed CLI exposes --restricted. Whether that surface can satisfy a required enforced-permission grant is an unmade adapter decision (B06/B07).
Effort now reaches the CLI: CompletionSpec.effort_args carries the router's `--effort <value>` (P12A S2). The values were read from --help, not exercised in a paid turn.

A quota delta is not attributable to one invocation without measured isolation; the shared account is written to by concurrent human use (B02). 2.1.268 populating resets_at and seven_day narrows the missing-data half of this, not the attribution half.

Subscription terms and the permitted-automation boundary were not verified. The standing mitigation is the credential-boundary invariant: invoke the installed CLI under its own login and never repurpose its credentials as an API transport.
records.notes: The CLI reports a list-price USD estimate per call. That is not evidence of a subscription charge and must not be converted into one. Re-verified at 2.1.268: the 2.1.263 row's null resets_at and null seven_day were a property of that version's telemetry, not of the reading method — both are populated now. Re-verified again at 2.1.269 during P02: the control set (--effort, --model, --restricted, --resume), the declared capability set and the quota surface are byte-identical to the 2.1.268 reading — five_hour.resets_at, the seven_day window and the context reading are all populated. A re-pin on observation, not a version bump. Re-verified at 2.1.270 on 2026-09-13 the same way: help_controls, maestro_capabilities and the usage field set match the 2.1.269 reading.

records.subject: codex
records.verified_by: local blind-spot audit (scripts/graph_blind_spot_audit.py) re-run against the installed CLI on 2026-09-11 — --help inspection plus repeated Maestro telemetry reads (3 audit runs, 3 direct app-server calls), no agent turn

effort_control.observed: still no --effort flag at 0.154.0; effort is `-c model_reasoning_effort=<value>` (the ~/.codex/config.toml key). Values are ~/.codex/models_cache.json supported_reasoning_levels on 2026-09-15, intersected across gpt-6-astra / gpt-5.6-sol / terra / luna (`ultra` is not on luna, so it is excluded).

quota_surface.windows: 300 and 10080 both present with used_pct and a real resets_at epoch
quota_surface.reliability: NOT reliably available at 0.154.0 — one of three audit runs returned no sample at all from the app-server fallback while three consecutive direct calls in the same minute each returned one
quota_surface.assessment: still the best-instrumented of the three on this host when it answers, but a None is now a normal outcome and callers must treat it as 'not measurable', never as 'no limits'

configured_tuple_observed.note: the host's ~/.codex/config.toml moved from gpt-5.6-sol to gpt-5.6-terra between the two verifications; a host setting, not a CLI change

open_questions: PATH still holds a second codex at 0.122.0 (/usr/bin/codex); /home/dan/.local/bin/codex at 0.154.0 is the first match. registry.resolve_binary pins the first PATH match, so a PATH change would silently swap the version this row was verified against. Unchanged from the 0.153.4 row and re-confirmed on 2026-09-11.

Acquisition is no longer fully solved: the account-level usage read intermittently returns None at 0.154.0 (1 of 3 audit runs). Whether that is an app-server start race, a timeout, or a changed surface is unknown, and it matters because a None must not be read as an empty limits map (B02).
Attribution is not solved: the five-hour window moved 84% to 89% during a paired sample in which zero Codex tasks were launched (B02).
Effort is delivered as a config key, not a flag. Nothing may assume a --effort surface here, and no effort label may be mapped to another vendor's without a measured mapping (B06).
Subscription terms and the permitted-automation boundary were not verified; the credential-boundary invariant is the standing mitigation.
records.notes: Re-verified at 0.154.0 on 2026-09-11. The one behavioural change the re-verification found is the intermittent null usage sample; the control surface and declared capabilities are unchanged from 0.153.4.
